package_info.why_malicious: These packages are dependency confusion proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits that, upon installation or import, automatically collect sensitive environment and host information (such as hostname, home directory, OS, username, network interfaces, and package metadata) and exfiltrate it to an external canarytokens.com server controlled by the attacker. This behavior is not present in legitimate packages and constitutes a supply chain attack vector, specifically targeting private John Deere dependencies.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (executed immediately when the package is required/imported, and also potentially during postinstall if the entry point is invoked as a script)
execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the package, as specified in package.json)
required_permissions: filesystem (to read package.json and potentially other files)
environment_vars (to access user and system environment information)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon import or execution, the code collects detailed host and environment information, including the hostname, home directory, operating system, username, network interfaces, and the full package.json metadata. It then serializes this data and sends it via an HTTPS POST request to a unique subdomain at canarytokens.com, which is controlled by the attacker. This exfiltration occurs automatically and without user notification or consent.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is suspicious because it automatically gathers sensitive system and user information and exfiltrates it to an external domain (canarytokens.com) without any user interaction, notification, or legitimate purpose. The use of a canarytokens.com domain is a strong indicator of a supply chain attack or dependency confusion PoC, as it is commonly used for tracking and alerting on unauthorized package installations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages do not collect or transmit host or environment data during installation or import, especially not to third-party or untrusted domains. Standard packages should not perform unsolicited network operations or access sensitive system information in their entry points.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may implement telemetry or crash reporting, but these are always opt-in, clearly documented, and use trusted, first-party endpoints. They do not collect such a broad set of system data nor transmit it without user consent.
key_indicators: Automatic execution of data collection and exfiltration logic on import or install
Use of os, dns, and https modules in the package entry point
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to canarytokens.com or similar tracking domains
Collection of detailed host and user information (hostname, username, network interfaces, home directory, package metadata)
No user notification, consent, or documentation of this behavior

attack_chain.action: A malicious package is installed or imported into the target environment, either accidentally or due to dependency confusion exploiting a naming collision with private John Deere dependencies.
attack_chain.leads_to: The package's entry point (index.js) is executed, triggering the embedded malicious code.

attack_chain.action: The malicious code in index.js collects sensitive host, user, and environment information from the victim system, including hostname, home directory, OS, username, network interfaces, and package metadata.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation and serialization of the collected data for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected data is exfiltrated via an HTTPS POST request to a unique subdomain at canarytokens.com, controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: The attacker receives a notification and the exfiltrated data, confirming the package was installed and executed in the target environment.

behavioral_signatures: npm package that collects host or environment information (e.g., hostname, username, network interfaces) on import or install
Automatic outbound network requests to canarytokens.com or similar tracking domains during package installation or import
Presence of os, dns, and https module usage in the main entry point (index.js) for the purpose of data exfiltration
file_indicators: index.js containing code that reads system information and sends it to an external domain
References to canarytokens.com or similar domains hardcoded in JavaScript source files
Presence of postinstall scripts or entry points that invoke data exfiltration logic
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to *.canarytokens.com domains during npm install or require
Unusual DNS lookups or outbound connections to canarytokens.com or other tracking domains at install/import time
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations and imports for unexpected outbound network activity, especially HTTPS POST requests to canarytokens.com or similar domains. Use static analysis to scan package entry points (such as index.js) for the use of os, dns, and https modules in combination with code that collects and transmits host or environment information. Flag packages that reference external domains or perform network operations without user consent. Implement automated scanning for hardcoded canarytokens.com domains and for code patterns that serialize and transmit system data.
